findings: Both full captures document the same Android Apps on Devices submission. The app developer finalizes the app, creates the app record in Dashboard with name/package, selects matching hardware, uploads the APK, supplies reviewer instructions when review is required, enters one or more contact email addresses, and submits it for review.

Stripe reports the result by email, Dashboard status or webhook. The approval event establishes permission to deploy, while rejection requires fixing the issue and resubmitting. The dashboard Events link provides event visibility. Approval and device deployment remain separate operations.

The November capture is full functional evidence corroborating May. Its only deploy-route change is lowercase URL casing, which maps to the separately evidenced API private-preview deployment guide. The current source lists workflow and both event identifiers accurately but omits meanings and omits the downstream route.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 1 and November 7 as the capture dates. In both, submission is required after finalizing the app, reviewer instructions are conditional, and upload is via the Dashboard in the described route.
Preserve assessment state and device deployment as distinct. The Submit page covers review status, and the separately routed API deploy guide carries its own private-preview access condition.
conflicts: The related Apps on Devices concept gives reviewer instructions without the conditional wording in both Submit captures and shortens the rejected event spelling. Keep both complete identifiers and the required-review condition where it summarizes submission.
The November API deployment hyperlink alone does not establish API access, API-only deployment or automatic device deployment after approval.

findings: Add the November corroborating raw and the corrected deploy next-step locator as navigation. Preserve the complete May capture and the dedicated app review route.
State the status consequences of each webhook and add a source-side return link to the Apps on Devices concept, which already links to this source.
conflicts: Keep conditional reviewer instructions and route eligibility to the separate review guide. Approval permits deployment, and the linked API deployment path remains a separate private preview.
source_assessments.reason: No November functional change warrants a rewrite. The corrected deployment route is useful navigation, and both reviewed raws support clarifying the existing summary's event outcomes and reciprocal links.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/submit, source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-submit accurately summarizes both full captures' Dashboard upload flow. After finalizing an Android app, its developer creates an app record with name and package, selects compatible devices, uploads the APK, adds reviewer instructions if review is required, enters one or more notification emails and submits it to Stripe (old raw lines 8-22, new raw lines 9-23). Stripe can report the review result by email, show the status on the Dashboard app details page, or send the full terminal.device_asset_version.app_review_approved or terminal.device_asset_version.app_review_rejected event to the merchant's webhook endpoint. Approval permits later deployment. Rejection requires the developer to fix and resubmit. The summary lists the channels and event names but omits these outcomes and the separate deploy route (old raw lines 24-41, new raw lines 25-42).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/submit, source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-submit merits a raw_reference update for the November 7 corroborating capture and corrected deployment link. Compared with May 1, the wording of the reviewer-instruction advice, list numerals and status-table spacing are presentation. The deployment hyperlink changes only deploy-with-API to deploy-with-api. Both dates retain compatible-device selection, conditional reviewer instructions, email/Dashboard/webhook status, approval for deployment and correction/resubmission after rejection (old raw lines 8-22, old raw lines 24-41, new raw lines 9-23, new raw lines 25-42). The separate November app-review guide raw/stripe-terminal-features-apps-on-devices-app-review-2026-11-07.md lines 9-15 qualifies non-P2PE Stripe reader, DevKit-only, and previously approved APK automated-approval cases. The separate API deployment guide raw/stripe-terminal-features-apps-on-devices-deploy-with-api-2026-11-07.md at line 15 identifies private preview access. The next-step URL change does not remove the Dashboard deployment route, establish universal API access, or turn an approval event into deployment. Add the return link to stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices and retain the distinct app review and deployment references.
